# FloodLens Lifelines - ML data report and Kill Test 1

*Generated by `src/08_report.py` from the pipeline outputs. No model was trained or tuned.*

**Usable-size check:** 236 usable gauges (>= 30 required) and 90 storm events (>= 5 required): both thresholds met.
**Window:** 2015-01-01 00:00 to 2023-01-31 23:00 UTC. The NWM v3.0 retrospective ends 2023-02-01, so the requested end of 2023-12-31 was truncated for *everything* (observed data, NWM, labels).

## Headline

- Kill Test 1 (pre-set bar: PR-AUC >= 2x base rate) passes on every subset with both scores on the pre-registered all-hours population. **Read the caveats before trusting this**:
  1. Positives are rare (base rates 0.5-7%), so a 2x bar is easy to clear. Absolute precision is what matters operationally.
  2. Most positive hours occur while a gauge is *already* above flood stage (persistence). Restricted to **onset** hours (gauge not yet at flood stage), PR-AUC falls to 0.02-0.03 on all non-Florence data and recall at 50% precision is about 0. The 2x bar is still cleared (13-21x base), but the practical signal is weak.
  3. The Florence "event" is a 54-day chain (Florence + Michael + slow river recession) under the 5-day rule; the test set is one event, so its confidence interval is a gauge bootstrap, not an event bootstrap.
- Hazard-ladder level A-D: **not reported** - the ladder definition was not in the task. Give me the definition and I will map the result.

### Datum check
USGS gage height vs NWS stage at up to 5 of the largest post-2007 NWPS crests per gauge (`datum_check_events.csv`). Crests dated only to a day (00:00Z) used a +-36 h window, others +-3 h. Pass: >= 2 comparable crests and median |difference| <= 0.5 ft. Excluded gauges and reasons: `datum_exclusions.csv`.

| datum_reason | gauges |
|---|---|
| fewer than 2 comparable crest events | 22 |
| median |USGS-NWS| > 0.5 ft | 6 |
| no NWPS crest with USGS gage height | 27 |

(The first pass used a +-3 h window for every crest and a >= 3-crest rule; it excluded 134 of 233 gauges, mostly artifacts of the window. Fixed and rerun.)

## 2. Events (statewide, new event after >= 5 days with no exceedance at any official gauge)
90 events, 78928 exceedance gauge-hours (`events.csv`, one row per event with gauges and hours). Named:

| event_id | start | end | n_gauges_exceeding | exceedance_gauge_hours | name |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 19 | 2016-09-21 17:00:00+00:00 | 2016-10-23 11:00:00+00:00 | 53 | 5662 | Matthew (Oct 2016) |
| 39 | 2018-09-13 17:00:00+00:00 | 2018-11-06 03:00:00+00:00 | 85 | 7448 | Florence (Sept 2018) |

Florence: the chain does not break for 54 days (85 gauges exceed). The 5-day rule merges Florence with Hurricane Michael (Oct 2018) and the recession. Under the rules as specified this whole window is TEST, plus 7 days before and after as buffer. Matthew likewise runs 2016-09-21 to 2016-10-23.

```
LEAKAGE TESTS

[PASS] no event_id spans two cv folds
[PASS] no holdout gauge has a trainval row
[PASS] pilot gauges in train >= half of pilot gauges
[PASS] no trainval/unseen row inside test+buffer window
[PASS] features recomputed from data <= t match table (40 gauges x 8 hours x 3 features), mismatches=0
[PASS] exceed_next_6h equals max stage over (t, t+6] only (10 gauges x 20 hours), mismatches=0
[PASS] nwm_flow_pctile reference = TRAIN hours only (unseen gauges: unseen hours), mismatched gauges=0
```

## 5. Kill Test 1
Score -> target `exceed_next_12h` (1 h and 6 h in `kill_test_1.csv`). Both scores scored on identical rows (gauges with a Q_fs). Block bootstrap by event_id cluster (B = 1000); TEST and the Florence-pilot subset are one event, so TEST resamples gauges and the Florence-pilot interval is n/a. Base rate = prevalence. Bar fixed in advance: PR-AUC >= 2x base rate.

**Verdict: PASS on the pre-set bar for all subsets and both scores.** Honest reading: the NWM-to-flood-stage ratio ranks hours that are already flooding or about to; it ranks true onset hours poorly (recall at 50% precision about 0 on non-Florence onset). `baseline_ratio` is better than `nwm_flow_pctile` for all-hours but not for onset or pilot. Where the point estimate falls outside its bootstrap CI (some onset rows), a few events dominate - treat as unstable.

## 6. Limitations
- NWM retrospective is a free-running hindcast driven by observed forcing, **no data assimilation**, so it is not a forecast; real lead-time skill needs the operational/forecast products.
- Hourly alignment: observations are binned to [h, h+1) labelled by hour start (stage = max, discharge = mean); NWM is the instantaneous top-of-hour value. A sub-hour offset is possible.
- Unseen-gauge `baseline_ratio` uses a Q_fs from the gauge's own observations (non-test hours), and trainval Q_fs/percentile come from the same hours later scored (no model, but not out-of-sample). Optimistic for the "ungauged" story.
- Q2 proxy threshold = median of pre-2015 annual peaks (>= 10 peaks), not Log-Pearson III; compared against hourly-mean discharge. Gauges without >= 10 pre-2015 peaks have no proxy label.
- Merged mega-events (Florence+Michael, Matthew, several winter chains) are long; "event" bootstrap clusters are coarse and the quiet stretches are clusters too.
- One reach (Catawba below Lookout Shoals Dam, 0214244102) has no NWM output at all (regulated); its features are NaN.
- The 5-day statewide gap rule groups unrelated simultaneous storms; no storm-type attribution.
- 32 candidate gauges are not in the NWM channel network (RouteLink gages or NWPS reachId) and are absent.
- The hand-built `gauges.csv` was not available.

## 7. Verified vs assumed
**Verified (checked against live sources in this run):** USGS OGC API base `https://api.waterdata.usgs.gov/ogcapi/v1/` (collections, queryables, pagination, 1000 req/h quota); NWPS gauge fields incl. `usgsId`, `reachId`, flood categories, historic crests; `chrtout.zarr` layout (time x feature chunks of 672 x 30000), coverage ends 2023-02-01 00:00, `gage_id`/`order`/lat/lon coordinates; NWPS `reachId` equals the RouteLink match for every gauge with both; feature recomputation from data <= t; label windows; TRAIN-only percentile reference.
**Assumed:** the embedded `gage_id` coordinate equals the official NWM v3.0 RouteLink `gages` field (not independently diffed against the standalone RouteLink file); NWPS minor-category stage is "flood stage"; 0.5 ft median tolerance means a consistent datum; 5 km distance tolerance; NWM reach lat/lon is representative of the reach; 15-minute/5-minute USGS data are approved/provisional as served (qualifier not filtered).
